notes: The 1966 volume of the Recreation and Park Commission. Curated: namings (including John F. Kennedy Drive's list), the Washington Square garage, gifts and design approvals for Dolores Park, Strybing Arboretum and the Japantown Peace Plaza.

coverage.remaining: Routine items not curated. Not placed: Main Drive in Golden Gate Park named John F. Kennedy Drive (Res 6905; no page), Wurster, Bernardi and Emmons' road for the Sutro Baths housing (Jul 28; no page), the Civic Center Plaza redesign (Halprin; no page), the Junior League Room at the Senior Center (invitation only).
coverage.note: Dated by meeting openers; the Oct 13 meeting's later pages carry 10/12 footers. Curated list F1966.py.

findings.address_as_written: Proposed tennis courts on top of the Lombard Street Reservoir
findings.description: On its naming committee's recommendation, the Recreation and Park Commission named the tennis courts to be built on top of the Lombard Street Reservoir the Alice Marble Tennis Courts, for the San Francisco-born world and national champion.

citation.label: Minutes of the Recreation and Park Commission, January 27, 1966, Resolution No. 6568

findings.description: After two hearings at which North Beach merchants backed the plan and the Telegraph Hill Dwellers, the Sierra Club and the architect Helen Douglass French opposed it, the Recreation and Park Commission approved in principle a garage under Washington Square, proposed with Wilsey-Hamm and Blair as engineers, provided the Parking Authority and the Board of Supervisors found it feasible, and asked to review the plans for the restored park on top.

findings.address_as_written: Plaza at Mission Dolores Park for the Liberty Bell, gift of the Mexican government
findings.description: The Recreation and Park Commission approved Donald Clark's final design for a plaza in Mission Dolores Park around a replica of the bell Father Miguel Hidalgo rang at Dolores, Mexico, in 1810, a gift of the Mexican government; it had accepted the gift in principle in April.
